comment: Tool names the OFFICIAL hosted Miro MCP server (mcp.miro.com) registers, enumerated via an authenticated claude.ai connector session. The README's Official-vs-Community comparison cites len(tools). Re-enumerate monthly or on Miro announcements (bead 6kn); this needs an interactive authenticated session, so it stays manual — CI cannot do it. Diff against this file and update both it and README on drift.

history.note: board_trash and space_delete removed — the surface's only hard-destructive verbs

all five code_widget_* tools removed; canvas_search, canvas_load_format_skill and content_item_list_roles added. layout_* still registered but self-describe as deprecated in favour of the canvas tools

61 -> 45, the largest drop yet and all removals: board_list_items, board_show, context_explore, context_get, all three diagram_*, all three doc_*, all four layout_*, import-claude-design-from-url, record_ui_feedback. One coherent story rather than attrition - every removed tool is a content read/write path superseded by canvas_*, and the server's own connection instructions now lead with Canvas Composer SVG as 'Miro's unified interaction/representation protocol for the canvas'. The 09-09 pass predicted this: layout_* were already self-describing as deprecated in favour of canvas.
history.channel: Claude Code MCP client against mcp.miro.com, scopes boards:read boards:write openid email
history.caveat: Prior passes enumerated via a claude.ai connector; this one used Claude Code, so a scope-gated difference cannot be fully excluded. Evidence against that reading: every write tool survives (board_create, space_create, table_create, section_create, comment_create) while reads were removed, which is the opposite of what scope gating produces. Re-enumerate via claude.ai next pass to close it out.
